result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. Nothing was committed. The full offline suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`), including the new tests.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: the record has a new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor is kept and defaults to 30, so the many existing call sites in tests and the demo still compile.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms. Every supplier read now selects the column, including the four listings you named (by name, by country, by minimum rating, `findSupplierById`). I also added it to the supplier reads inside other queries (purchase-order lines, performance, spending, single-source categories). Otherwise those would have silently reported 30 days for every supplier. This goes slightly beyond the four listings you named.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: two new tests. One follows your example: 45 days at registration, then renegotiated to 14, checked in all four listings. The other checks the 30-day default.

There is no supplier service class, so the terms are entered through `DataStore.createSupplier` and `updateSupplier`, like the other supplier fields.
